title: Restriction to the generic fibre detects sections on a reduced horizontal source
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $S$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], and $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Suppose every generic point of every irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] maps to $\xi$. Let $V\subseteq X$ be any open subset whose underlying topological space is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), and give $V$ its open-subscheme structure. Put $V_\xi=V\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field]. Then the canonical pullback homomorphism $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(V_\xi,\mathcal O_{V_\xi})$ is injective. The source $X$ may be reducible, $V$ may be empty, and no properness, Noetherian, or finite-presentation assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, label lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal, proof: reducedness and dominance of all component generic points; generic-fibre restriction subargument made explicit. Nilpotent-section detection is the surjectivity paragraph of Tag 03GY, label lemma-stein-universally-closed.

proof.text: Write $i:V_\xi\to V$ for the fibre projection and let $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$ satisfy $i^*a=0$. If $\eta\in V$ is the generic point of an irreducible component of $X$, then $f(\eta)=\xi$. The fibre-point description [def-pc-scheme-fibre] gives a point $z\in V_\xi$ with $i(z)=\eta$. By the definition of the residue-field map [def-weil-residue-field], evaluation of $i^*a$ at $z$ is the image of $a(\eta)$ under $\kappa(\eta)\to\kappa(z)$. A unital homomorphism of fields is injective: its kernel is an ideal and cannot contain $1$. Thus $a(\eta)=0$.

source.place: Tags 01K0 (definition-fibre), 01K1 (lemma-fibre-topological), and residue-field maps of locally ringed spaces; elementary evaluation argument

proof.text: The nonvanishing set $D(a)=\{x\in V:a(x)\ne0\}$ is open in $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function]. If $x\in D(a)$, choose an irreducible component $C$ of $X$ containing $x$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], and its generic point $\eta$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Since $x\in C=\overline{\{\eta\}}$, every open neighbourhood of $x$, in particular $D(a)$, contains $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Hence $\eta\in V$ and $a(\eta)\ne0$, contradicting Step 1. Consequently $D(a)=\varnothing$, so $a(x)=0$ for every $x\in V$.

source.place: Tags 01HZ (lemma-f-open), 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); Topology Tag 004W (lemma-irreducible), together with the definition of closure

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qc-scheme-vanishing-section-nilpotent] to the open subscheme $V$: it is quasi-compact by hypothesis and Step 2 gives vanishing at every residue field. Thus $a^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$. The reducedness equivalence in [def-pc-reduced-scheme] says that $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$ is reduced, hence $a=0$. For two sections with equal pullbacks apply this argument to their difference. This proves injectivity, also when $V$ is empty, since the argument never chooses a point unless one is given.
